executive_summary: Collection window February 22-28, 2028: London Fashion Week Fall/Winter 2028 women's shows, on the calendar confirmed in the 2028-02-21 report, took place within this window. Simone Rocha's own site published the house's runway lookbook for its Fall/Winter 2028 London show, and vogue.com independently reviewed the same show, both identifying a pearl-trimmed puff-sleeve dress -- a dress with an exaggerated, rounded puffed sleeve construction finished with a dense pearl-bead trim at the cuff and neckline -- as a recurring construction across multiple looks. This is treated as genuine cross-sector corroboration, applying the identical reasoning already used for the 2028-01-24 Louis Vuitton, 2028-01-31 Dior, 2028-02-14 Proenza Schouler, and 2028-02-21 Khaite signals: one designer_origin source (the house's own lookbook) and one editorial source doing independent runway-review reporting, not a restatement of the house's own materials. Separately, Camera Nazionale della Moda Italiana, Milan Fashion Week's governing body, published its official calendar for Fall/Winter 2028 women's Milan Fashion Week this window, the next leg of the international fashion-month sequence following London's close, and wwd.com independently reported on the announcement with added confirmed-participant detail beyond a restatement of the CNMI's own release -- the same fact pattern already applied to the 2028-02-21 BFC/vogue.com London calendar-confirmation signal, the 2028-02-07 CFDA/wwd.com New York calendar-confirmation signal, and the 2028-01-10 FHCM/wwd.com Paris menswear calendar-confirmation signal. Per precedent 6 in the confidence-discipline precedents doc, these two signals' same-week co-occurrence is not treated as cross-sector corroboration between them; each is derived only from sources that address it directly. The Khaite cantilevered-shoulder-blazer thread, the Proenza Schouler spiral-seam-wrap-coat thread, the resort 2028 puffer-shell skirt thread, the resale-demand signal on structured waist-tailoring, the obi-sash cocoon coat thread, and the opera-glove/'restraint dressing' thread all produced no new development this window and are not carried forward again absent fresh movement. The Margiela raw-edge thread remains closed out as of 2027-10-18. Met Gala 2027, Wales Bonner, and CFDA's Fashion Fund/Awards remain untracked going forward per standing convention.
